# Chapter 9 — Real-Time Intelligence and Eventstreams Under the Domain Hierarchy

::: {.callout-note}
## In this chapter
The data plane in Chapter 5 was a data-at-rest plane — mirrored SQL estates and lakehouse items under a domain. Fabric Real-Time Intelligence adds a data-in-motion plane: eventstreams, eventhouses, and KQL databases that ingest and serve streaming data. This chapter extends the domain-and-OrgPath model to those streaming items, so real-time workloads inherit the same organizational governance, default sensitivity context, and drift detection as the batch estate — and so streaming data does not become the ungoverned seam that escapes the substrate.
:::

## The Data-in-Motion Plane Chapter 5 Did Not Cover

Establish the new surface: eventstreams, eventhouses, and KQL databases are first-class Fabric items but they were outside Chapter 5's mirroring-and-domain treatment. Without explicit governance they ingest and serve data under no organizational anchor — the classic ungoverned seam.

## Streaming Items as Domain-Assigned Workspace Items

Apply the existing model: real-time items live in workspaces, and workspaces are domain-assigned in Chapter 5. Show that the domain assignment already covers streaming items by inheritance, and identify what does *not* inherit automatically and must be reconciled explicitly.

## Default Sensitivity Context and Authorization on Streaming Data

Address the data-protection question: streaming data needs the same default sensitivity context and authorization model as the batch estate. Describe how the domain's context propagates to eventhouse/KQL data and where Purview classification reaches (and does not yet reach) real-time items in GCC Moderate.

## Reconciling and Auditing Real-Time Items by OrgPath

Mechanism: extend the domain-assignment reconciliation job to enumerate real-time items and confirm each carries the domain its workspace claims, emitting `DRIFT-PROVENANCE` for any eventhouse or KQL database whose assignment is missing or mismatched.

## Boundary Caveats and Cross-Reference to Chapter 7

Close with boundary reality: Real-Time Intelligence feature availability and Purview integration for streaming items differ in GCC Moderate. Cross-reference Chapter 7's boundary-caveats treatment so the streaming story shares the same boundary discipline as the rest of the Azure SSOT stack.
